question: Launch windows open when Earth and a target planet line up right. For which planet do they come round least often?
answer: Mars. A window returns each time one planet laps the other, and Earth gains on Mars slowest of all: every 780 days, 26 months. Neptune barely moves, so Earth realigns with it every 367 days; Venus returns every 19 months. Mars, the neighbour, is the one that makes missions wait longest.
move: How often two things meet depends on their difference, not their distance.
trap: Neptune, the farthest planet, seems the hardest to line up with.
source: Curtis, Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students, 2020
reference: Curtis, Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students, 4th ed., Butterworth-Heinemann, 2020
